Maya: Quick Q — thinking through client backpressure for per-route quotas. When should SDKs treat a soft signal (200 + hint header) as advisory vs a hard 429 that needs immediate retry/backoff? :thinking:
Liam: Short answer: SDK should treat 200+hint as advisory only. 429 should always trigger retry/backoff logic.
Maya: Agree. For checkout flows we need stricter semantics though — user-perceived failures are bad. Want to make sure we document expectations.
Arjun: For critical routes (checkout, billing) prefer fail-fast 429s. Soft hints are for best-effort degradation (suggested throttling, local cache).
Zoe: Draft header examples below, trying to keep things human-readable: 
X-Redwood-Quota-Hint: bucket=checkout;allowance=20;window=60;mode=soft
X-Redwood-Quota-Burst: tokens=120;lease_ms=2000
Retry-After: 3
Liam: That format looks fine. key=value semi-colon separated. SDKs can parse into a map. Keep it optional.
Priya: SDK team: Implementation notes — we can expose two switchable behaviors: 1) advisory-only (emit telemetry + let app decide), 2) conservative (treat repeated hints as soft-limit and apply client-side backoff). We should also recommend jittered exponential backoff if an SDK chooses to delay.
Maya: Backcompat note: legacy clients will ignore X-Redwood-* headers. We must not change 429 semantics for older clients. Headers must be opt-in parsing by new SDKs.
Arjun: Also request we include a small structured body on 429 with fields clients can rely on: "quota_bucket" and "recommended_wait_ms".
Maya: Example 429 body JSON: 
{"error":"rate_limited","quota_bucket":"checkout","recommended_wait_ms":1500}
Zoe: ops-bot: deploy scheduled to staging at 2025-08-14T14:00Z :rocket:
ops-bot: Canary will route 10% traffic to the variant that emits header hints. Watch for increased client telemetry.
Liam: Question: precedence between per-route and per-account quotas? Which one should the headers reflect?
Priya: We propose precedence: scope=route > scope=account > scope=global. Header should include scope, e.g., scope=route. That helps SDKs decide which hint to honor.
Maya: Agreed. Also flagging that we need clear server-side docs describing modes: soft vs hard enforcement, and how tokens/lease_ms map to burst windows.
Arjun: Tests to add: SDK unit tests asserting 200+hint doesn't throw, and 429 triggers retry/backoff. Also integration test where header is present but client is old (ignore) to ensure no regressions.
Zoe: I'll draft the spec text and include sample header parsing snippets for JS/Python SDKs.
Maya: Can we finalize header grammar here so I can open the PR? Proposed ABNF-ish: header := key=value(;key=value)* where keys: bucket, allowance (int), window (seconds), tokens (burst tokens), lease_ms, mode (soft|hard), scope (route|account|global).
Liam: One nit: prefer 'allowance' -> 'allowed' to keep names short, but both ok.
Maya: Good call. I'll use 'allowed' in the PR.
Priya: SDK team will implement advisory parsing and a config flag `honor_quota_hints` defaulting to false for backward compatibility.
Maya: Thanks all — sounds like consensus. I'll open the spec PR and tag SDK + ops for rollout checklist. :thumbsup:
Liam: LGTM
Arjun: +1
Zoe: Ping me when PR is up, I'll add examples.
Priya: Will add SDK unit tests after PR merges.
